answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism is bonded identity with slow-maturing reputation. Each agent locks a timber-like stack of tokens as a bond: affordable once for an honest operator, but each forged identity multiplies the cost. Reputation accrues only through attested useful work over time, so a fresh sybil army begins at the zenith of zero trust and earns nothing. Misbehavior slashes the bond. An attacker keeps funding and aging identities like the burning tail of a comet: costs scale with identities while rewards stay flat, pricing sybils out of profitability.
